newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Diesel up despite several offers.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Diesel up despite several offers.

text.p: Gas oil prices rose and the recent bullish trend held precariously intact after levels refused to come under pressure from a spate of aggressive offers, traders said on Monday.

At least four offers for late March to early April cargoes were offered in the Singapore spot market with prices ranging between $27.30 to $27.70 per barrel against a bid from a Singapore trader at $26.80-$27.00.

A deal was finally transacted with the Singapore trader buying a 220,000 barrels cargo loading end March at $27 per barrel from a Chinese bunker trader and another 100,000 barrels for March 31-April 4 at $27.30 from a Swiss trader.
"Bargain hunters were seeking to sell their wet barrels, taking opportunity of the recent price hike," said one trader.
Most traders said the market is artificially supported.
"If the local trader has not emerged to soak up the excess barrels the market would not be so bullish," said a western trader in Singapore.
"If the local trader has over two million barrels worth of swaps, he must be hedging a physical position worth about the same volume, meaning the market has alot of supplies," he added.
Traders said the intermonth March/April spread has widened to around $2.40 in the swaps market, a situation unseen for a long time as the usual spread was an average of $1.00-$1.50 per barrel.
They said as more arbitrage cargoes, fixed earlier, head towards the East, prices should ease.

In the jet fuel market, two 100,000 barrels cargoes were traded at $28.50 and $28.00 per barrel for March 25-28 and March 31-April 4 lifting respectively. Both were purchased by the same Singapore trader who had bought the gas oil supplies. The earlier cargo was sold by a European major while a Mideast trader sold the later one.
Earlier in the day, the same Mideast trader purchased 140,000 barrels from a major at 70 cents per barrel premium to Singapore spot quotes for March 23-25 loading.
Traders said the premium was considered high as the last deal traded a week ago was at a 40-50 cents premium.
Traders said the Mideast buyer could be covering a short position when he had sold a 100,000 barrels parcel at $26.60 earlier this month.
The Singapore trader confirmed its jet and gasoil deals but would not comment on his position.
